q: In 1993, which grunge frontman fell off a 30-foot speaker tower at an outdoor festival in Europe, landed in the mud, and finished the song without missing a beat?
fact: Vedder was notorious for death-defying stage climbing at Pearl Jam shows, scaling scaffolding and stage roofs before staging colossal stage dives into packed stadium crowds.

q: Which famous comedian was arrested in 1972 at Milwaukee’s Summerfest for performing his legendary routine "Seven Words You Can Never Say on Television"?
fact: Carlin was arrested for disturbing the peace after reciting his iconic profanity monologue; a Wisconsin judge later dismissed the charges, ruling the words were protected artistic expression.

q: What did pop legend Prince do when invited to play a concert at the White House for President Barack Obama and 500 guests in 2015?
options: Demanded the entire Oval Office be draped in purple velvet
Performed a surprise, unannounced two-hour private show alongside Stevie Wonder
Refused to walk on the White House carpets unless they were steamed
Requested that secret service agents play brass horns on stage
fact: In June 2015, Prince and Stevie Wonder played an unannounced, legendary private concert in the East Room for the Obamas and 500 close friends that was not listed on any public schedule.

q: Which Hollywood icon famously owned a pet raven named Grip that he taught to talk and steal small silver coins from his houseguests?
fact: Dickens loved his pet raven Grip, who could mimic voices and peck guests' shins; after Grip died, Dickens had him taxidermied, inspiring Edgar Allan Poe's famous poem "The Raven".

q: In 1988, which actor was involved in a high-speed police chase on a Harley-Davidson in Malibu that ended with him crashing into a eucalyptus tree?
fact: In December 1988, Busey suffered a catastrophic motorcycle crash without a helmet in Los Angeles, fracturing his skull and undergoing emergency neurosurgery, which permanently altered his behavior.

q: What did eccentric director Stanley Kubrick do when a script supervisor pointed out a continuity error during the filming of "Eyes Wide Shut"?
options: Promoted the supervisor to second-unit director on the spot
Forced the crew to dismantle the entire set and rebuild it from scratch
Fired the supervisor and banned all mirrors from the set
Stared at the supervisor for ten minutes in complete silence before resuming
fact: Kubrick's legendary obsession with technical perfectionism led to multiple halts and exhaustive reshoots over his record-breaking 400-day shoot of "Eyes Wide Shut".

q: Which famous hip-hop group threw a 20-foot motorized inflatable penis onto the stage during their 1987 "Licensed to Ill" arena tour?
fact: The Beastie Boys' chaotic early tour featured an enormous hydraulic prop rising through the stage floor, sparking threats of obscenity arrests from local police departments across America.

q: In 1969, which Hollywood screen legend was pulled over by police in Bel Air for driving his sports car backward down the street at 40 miles per hour?
fact: McQueen's reckless driving escapades were legendary around Los Angeles; he frequently tested high-performance sports cars and motorcycles in dangerous maneuvers across residential streets.

q: What bizarre gift did rock legend Alice Cooper receive from surrealist master Salvador Dalí when they met in New York in 1973?
options: A plaster sculpture of a brain topped with an éclair and live crawling ants
A signed jar containing Dalí’s clipped fingernails
fact: Dalí was fascinated by Cooper's stage theatrics; the two collaborated on the world’s first 3D holographic portrait, and Dalí presented Cooper with a sculpture of a brain crowned with a pastry and ants.

q: Which celebrated actor was expelled from the American Academy of Dramatic Arts in 1953 for riding a donkey into the conservatory’s main library?
fact: Rip Torn's explosive, anarchic behavior began in his early training years, leading to multiple reprimands and dismissals before he achieved acclaim on Broadway.

q: In 1981, which movie star tackled an intruder inside his Los Angeles mansion, holding the burglar at gunpoint while wearing only silk pajama bottoms?
fact: Reynolds confronted a break-in suspect in his Beverly Hills home, holding him on the ground at gunpoint until LAPD patrol units arrived to arrest the intruder.

q: What did British eccentric Keith Moon do when he was told that his favorite London pub was closing for the afternoon?
options: Bought the pub on the spot and declared it open 24 hours a day
Chained himself to the bar counter and swallowed the key
Smashed the front doors with a sledgehammer
Poured ten gallons of draft stout into the street drain
fact: Moon often solved closing-time disputes by offering publicans cash buyouts or paying massive tabs to keep establishments open exclusively for his entourage.

q: In 1994, which pop star was detained by customs in Frankfurt after attempting to smuggle an endangered baby tiger cub in a Louis Vuitton sports bag?
fact: Rapper Vanilla Ice had an exotic animal menagerie in Florida that included wallaroos, lynxes, and tigers, running into multiple wildlife permit violations with state authorities.

q: Which Hollywood screen siren famously had all the plumbing fixtures in her Beverly Hills mansion plated in 24-karat gold so her bathwater would "feel softer"?
fact: Mansfield’s famous 40-room "Pink Palace" on Sunset Boulevard was legendary for its pink quartz, cupid-shaped fountains, heart-shaped swimming pool, and gold-plated bathroom fittings.

q: In 1987, why was Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash escorted out of the Beverly Hills Hotel by armed security?
options: He brought a live 6-foot mountain lion into his penthouse suite
He hallucinated "predator monsters" from heroin withdrawal and ran naked through the glass lobby doors
He threw an electric Marshall amplifier through a third-story plate-glass window
He tried to pay for a $12,000 bar tab with three stolen Gibson Les Paul guitars
fact: During a severe overdose hallucination, Slash believed invisible monsters with dreadlocks were pursuing him; he leapt through a glass door, hid behind a maid's cart, and ran naked into a nearby golf course.

q: In 1969, why did Jimi Hendrix spend several hours under arrest in a Canadian jail cell after arriving at Toronto International Airport?
options: Customs officials discovered packets of heroin and hashish inside his travel bag
He set his passport on fire with lighter fluid at the immigration desk
He punched a photographer who tried to pull his military jacket off
He refused to hand over his custom white Fender Stratocaster for agricultural x-raying
fact: Hendrix was formally charged with drug trafficking in Toronto; he was acquitted after successfully arguing to the jury that a fan had tossed the unknown contraband into his bag without his knowledge.

q: What did actor Christopher Walken famously make Christopher Nolan do when they met to discuss a potential movie role?
options: Meet him in an empty kitchen and cook a pot of spaghetti pomodoro together in total silence
Read the script out loud while doing tap-dancing steps
Hand over the script only on yellow paper typed on a mechanical Smith Corona
Sign a pledge promising no soundstage air conditioning would exceed 68 degrees
fact: Walken is an obsessive amateur chef who famously prefers conducting business meetings around his kitchen stove, insisting collaborators chop garlic and prep meals before discussing film scripts.

q: In 1974, during an intense creative block while composing "Young Americans", what did David Bowie famously do for days in his Philadelphia hotel suite?
options: Drew charcoal occult circles on the parquet floor and refused to let anyone open the curtains
Ate only canned peaches while playing the saxophone facing a mirror
Painted all the furniture and television sets stark silver to reflect lunar energy
Recorded 48 continuous hours of room ambient silence on quarter-inch reel tape
fact: Bowie’s mid-70s occult fascinations involved heavy rituals, keeping his blinds drawn at all times, drawing defensive esoteric glyphs on walls and floors, and believing Los Angeles and Philadelphia were psychic traps.

q: Which iconic British musician was arrested in 1967 at Keith Richards' country home "Redlands" after police found him in possession of four amphetamine tablets known as "Minims"?
fact: The notorious Redlands drug bust targeted Mick Jagger and Keith Richards; Jagger was sentenced to three months in prison for possessing legal travel pills bought in Italy, sparking The Times' famous editorial "Who breaks a butterfly on a wheel?".

q: Why was action star Dolph Lundgren almost prosecuted for manslaughter while filming the climax of "Rocky IV" (1985)?
options: He punched Sylvester Stallone so hard in the chest that Stallone's heart swelled and he was hospitalized in intensive care
He accidentally threw Carl Weathers through an actual soundstage electrical junction box
He knocked out three real professional stuntmen with a flying roundhouse kick
He choked a trainer with a sparring towel during an improvised take
fact: Stallone told Lundgren to punch him for real; Lundgren drove an uppercut into Stallone's ribs, slamming his heart against his breastbone (pericardial swelling) and requiring eight days in the ICU at St. John's Hospital.

q: In 1990, which celebrated hip-hop star survived getting shot nine times at point-blank range, but in 1994, which superstar survived being shot five times during a robbery inside Quad Studios in Manhattan?
fact: Tupac Shakur was ambushed and shot five times in the lobby of Quad Recording Studios in November 1994; he checked himself out of Bellevue Hospital less than 24 hours after emergency surgery.

q: What bizarre item did pop icon Cher keep in her bedroom closet during the 1980s that she claimed protected her home from unwanted psychic energy?
options: A life-sized taxidermied black panther with onyx eyes
An authentic medieval executioner's two-handed broadsword
A jar containing water from the River Jordan blessed by three priests
A mounted set of silver-tipped elk antlers
fact: Cher has long collected gothic antiques, including medieval tapestries, suits of armor, and authentic broadswords, keeping historical weapons near her master bed for both aesthetic and protective reasons.

q: In 1976, which rock frontman walked onto the stage of the Forum in Inglewood, California, wearing an apron, brandishing a meat cleaver, and chopping up a raw cabbage?
fact: Peter Gabriel’s avant-garde stage theatricality with Genesis featured elaborate surreal costumes—from the flower-headed man to Britannia to butchering produce—to embody the oddball narratives of their progressive songs.

q: Which Oscar-winning director made his entire production crew wear roller skates while filming an elaborate 360-degree party scene in 1977?
fact: For his satiric comedy "A Wedding" and related 1970s tracking shots, Robert Altman often equipped cinematographers and camera assistants with roller skates and skateboards to achieve smooth, sweeping mob moves.

q: In 1983, which actor broke his hand on the set of "The Outsiders" during a real rumble scene between the Greasers and the Socs?
fact: Francis Ford Coppola fostered real animosity between the two factions by housing them in different hotels; during the mud rumble scene, Cruise took a heavy blow, chipping a tooth and fracturing a bone in his hand.

q: What did British comedy legend Spike Milligan do when Prince Charles presented him with a prestigious lifetime comedy honor on live British television in 1994?
options: Called the Prince of Wales a "grovelling little bastard" directly into the microphone
Poured a pint of bitter over the Prince's ceremonial cufflinks
Pinched Prince Charles' ears and asked if they picked up satellite radio
Handed Prince Charles an unpeeled raw turnip from his tuxedo coat
fact: At the British Comedy Awards, when Prince Charles delivered a glowing televised tribute letter, Milligan glanced at the screen and cheerfully deadpanned: "Supposed to say something now... grovelling little bastard," leaving the audience in hysterics.

q: In 1995, which actress showed up at the Cannes Film Festival wearing an evening gown made entirely out of 85 expired American Express Gold Cards linked together by wire?
fact: Australian costume designer Lizzy Gardiner wore the iconic American Express card dress to accept the Best Costume Design Academy Award for "The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert" in March 1995.

q: Which iconic movie star had to be rescued from his sinking yacht off the coast of Catalina Island in 1968 while wearing nothing but his boxer shorts and an admiral's hat?
fact: John Wayne was a passionate mariner who lived aboard his converted World War II minesweeper, the "Wild Goose"; several near-miss grounding incidents off the California coast led to colorful Coast Guard rescue lore.

q: In 1978, which pop superstar was banned from entering Singapore because the government had strict laws prohibiting men from having long hair?
fact: Led Zeppelin was barred from disembarking their aircraft in Singapore in 1972 because customs and aviation authorities strictly enforced Operation Snip Snip, an anti-long-hair policy targeting male travelers.

q: What did eccentric actor Klaus Kinski do during the filming of Werner Herzog’s "Aguirre, the Wrath of God" in the Peruvian rainforest when extras made too much noise near his tent?
options: Fired three rifle bullets through the canvas wall of the hut, shooting off an extra's finger
Threw a crate of live piranhas into the communal bathing pool
Poured kerosene into the production generator to cut off all power
Chased the crew down the rapids with a machete naked
fact: Kinski was outraged by the noise of indigenous extras playing cards in a nearby tent; he grabbed a Winchester rifle and fired three shots into the hut, blowing off the tip of a man's finger.

q: In 1993, which Nirvana member was arrested for domestic assault after an argument with his wife over a cache of registered firearms kept in their Seattle home?
fact: Police responded to Cobain and Courtney Love's Seattle residence in June 1993 after neighbors reported shouting; officers confiscated three rifles, a semi-automatic handgun, and ammunition from the home.

q: Which Hollywood action hero worked as a professional grave digger in a cemetery in Munich before winning the Mr. Universe bodybuilding title?
fact: Several European strongmen held grueling physical labor jobs before fitness fame; German champion Ralf Moeller worked as a swimmer and lifeguard, while classic actor Rod Steiger worked in civil defense.

q: What bizarre habit did eccentric billionaire Howard Hughes develop while holed up in the penthouse of the Desert Inn in Las Vegas regarding his fingernails and toenails?
options: Refused to cut them for over a year, allowing them to curl into corkscrew claws
Had them polished with sterile silver paint to reflect bacterial radiation
Forced his aides to preserve every trimming inside numbered glass test tubes
fact: Hughes' severe mental decline led him to forbid anyone from trimming his nails for long periods; when aides were occasionally allowed to clip them, the trimmings had to be archived in sealed containers.

q: In 1982, which rock star broke into an off-limits room at a German castle hotel and was found the next morning asleep inside an authentic suit of 16th-century armor?
fact: Motörhead frontman Lemmy Kilmister was an avid collector of historical military artifacts, medieval swords, and regalia, frequently exploring old European hotels and sleeping surrounded by antique armor.

q: Which celebrated film director once bit an executive from Paramount Pictures on the arm during an argument over the budget for an epic western?
fact: Peckinpah was notorious for violent, alcohol-fueled rages on studio lots; during shouting matches with producers over cuts to "Major Dundee" and "Pat Garrett", physical brawling was common.

q: In 1973, what did legendary actor Marlon Brando do to paparazzo Ron Galella outside a restaurant in Chinatown, New York City?
options: Punched Galella in the face, breaking his jaw and knocking out five teeth
Smashed Galella's camera with a metal trash can lid
Had his bodyguards throw Galella into an open seafood tank
Offered Galella $10,000 in cash to delete the film rolls
fact: Galella jumped in front of Brando asking him to take off his sunglasses; Brando punched Galella in the jaw, severely injuring him and cutting his own hand, leading Galella to wear a football helmet around Brando thereafter.

q: What did actor Gary Oldman do to prepare for his role as Lee Harvey Oswald in Oliver Stone's "JFK" (1991)?
options: Tracked down Oswald's widow Marina and Oswald's two daughters to interview them in Texas
Lived in an unheated room in New Orleans on a budget of $2 a day
Fired thousands of rounds from an authentic 6.5mm Carcano rifle at a Texas firing range
fact: Oldman was relentless in his research, buying authentic vintage rifle models, practicing at Dallas gun ranges, shedding significant weight, and winning the trust of Marina Oswald Porter.

q: In 1986, which pop superstar broke her ankle during an acrobatic dance rehearsal for the "Control" tour, requiring her to perform early music videos seated on a stool?
fact: Janet Jackson worked through grueling dance regimens with choreographers Paula Abdul and Anthony Thomas, suffering repeated hairline ankle fractures and knee sprains during the album's launch.

q: Which iconic comedian was once challenged to a street fight outside a New York deli by mob enforcer "Crazy Joe" Gallo, only to defuse the hitman by doing an impromptu stand-up routine?
fact: Gallo approached Rickles at the Copacabana and demanded Rickles make him laugh; Rickles fearlessly roasted Gallo's mobster clothes, earning Gallo's lifelong respect and personal protection.

q: In 1999, which British rock star had his driver's license revoked after being caught driving 125 mph down the M4 motorway while balancing a bowl of cereal on his steering wheel?
fact: The Jamiroquai frontman and supercar enthusiast had multiple high-profile driving bans and court appearances across the UK for extreme speeding in Ferraris, Lamborghinis, and Aston Martins.

q: What did surrealist painter Salvador Dalí do when an American department store altered his window display without his permission in 1939?
options: Pushed a heavy acrylic bathtub through the plate-glass storefront window onto the street
Painted the exterior sidewalk with bright red surrealist lobsters
Poured 50 gallons of black paint over the mannequins
Handcuffed himself to the front revolving door
fact: Dalí was hired by Bonwit Teller in New York to design window displays; when the store modified his mannequin tub scene, Dalí flew into a rage, shoved the tub against the window, and crashed through the glass onto Fifth Avenue.

q: Which classic film actor was an Olympic-level fencer who performed all his own swordplay without doubles in swashbuckling films like "The Adventures of Robin Hood"?
fact: Rathbone was twice the British Army fencing champion and widely considered the greatest swordsman in Hollywood; in film climaxes, he routinely had to deliberately "lose" duels to actors with far less skill.

q: In 1975, which member of Pink Floyd showed up unannounced at Abbey Road Studios completely bald, having shaved off his eyebrows, while the band was mixing "Shine On You Crazy Diamond"?
fact: Barrett, who had left the band years earlier due to severe mental illness, wandered into Abbey Road during the mixing of the very song written about him; his bandmates were moved to tears before realizing who he was.

q: What bizarre thing did actor Nicolas Cage do during a guest appearance on the British talk show "Wogan" in 1990?
options: Cartwheeled onto the stage, performed karate kicks, took off his leather jacket, and threw cash into the audience
Sat on Terry Wogan's lap and recited Shakespeare in a vampire voice
Ate an entire raw habanero pepper and drank vinegar from a flask
Demanded that all the studio lights be switched off
fact: Promoting "Wild at Heart", a manic, leather-clad young Cage entered doing martial arts somersaults, ripped off his shirt to reveal an undershirt, and threw twenty-pound notes into the crowd.

q: In 1992, which rock icon survived a near-fatal fire at his London home after falling asleep on the sofa with a lit cigarette while wearing a nylon tracksuit?
fact: Ozzy suffered severe burns to his face, hands, and arms during a midnight blaze at his Buckinghamshire mansion, escaping with Sharon and their pets right before the room collapsed.

q: Which celebrated Hollywood actor was once caught by his high school principal running an illegal underground gambling ring out of the boys' locker room?
fact: Growing up in the tough Sunnyside neighborhood of Queens, James Caan was an energetic athlete and neighborhood hustler, running dice games and card rings before finding acting at Hofstra University.

q: In 1984, which country music legend played a concert at San Quentin State Prison, where an inmate in the front row was future country superstar Merle Haggard?
fact: Johnny Cash performed his historic New Year's Day concert at San Quentin in 1958; young inmate Merle Haggard was in the audience serving time for burglary, a life-changing moment that inspired him to pursue music.

q: What did actor Marlon Brando do when a director asked him to read the script for "The Teahouse of the August Moon" (1956)?
options: Ate three pages of the script dipped in soy sauce to show his disdain for the dialogue
Demanded to live in an authentic Okinawan hut built on the studio backlot
Spent two months speaking only through a translator
Insisted his pet raccoon be given an uncredited cameo
fact: Brando had an infamous habit of digesting script pages when displeased; on several occasions, he tore off dialogue corners, dipped them in condiments, and chewed them in front of terrified screenwriters.

q: In 1996, which rock singer was kicked off an international British Airways flight after trying to open the emergency exit door at 30,000 feet, thinking it was the bathroom?
fact: Happy Mondays frontman Shaun Ryder's extreme substance benders were notorious; during transatlantic flights, crew members had to physically tackle him away from aircraft doors and galley galleons.

q: Which Hollywood star was once an undercover bodyguard for the Beatles during their chaotic 1966 world tour stop in Los Angeles?
fact: Norris was a champion karate fighter in Southern California in the 1960s; celebrity security firms routinely hired him to provide physical escort protection for visiting rock icons and dignitaries.

q: In 1980, which comedian showed up to a live broadcast of "Fridays" (ABC's rival to SNL) and refused to read his cue cards, sparking an on-air physical brawl with the cast and crew?
fact: Kaufman broke character mid-sketch, stating "I can't play this, it's stupid"; co-star Michael Richards angrily slammed the cue cards on Kaufman's lap, and producer Jack Burns stormed the set, triggering a brawl.

q: What unusual object did rock legend Alice Cooper keep in his hotel room bathtub on every tour stop throughout the 1970s?
options: A live 10-foot boa constrictor named Kachina
A bucket of dry ice and cow bones
A custom electric guillotine blade wrapped in silk
fact: Cooper's stage boa constrictors (including Kachina and Yvonne) lived with him on the road; hotel maids were frequently startled to find giant snakes coiled peacefully inside Cooper's bathtubs.

q: Which Golden Age screen siren had an ironclad clause in her contract stating that she would never be filmed from the right side of her face?
fact: Colbert was so convinced that the right side of her face was unphotogenic that she insisted camera setups film only her left profile, forcing studios to redesign entire sets to accommodate her angles.

q: In 1994, which superstar actor paid $20,000 at an auction for a vintage silver cocktail shaker that had once belonged to mob boss Al Capone?
fact: Cage's fascination with Prohibition-era gangland history and crime memorabilia led him to assemble a private museum of artifacts once owned by prominent Chicago and New York mobsters.

q: Which classic rock singer was arrested in 1977 after riding a horse into a luxury hotel lobby in Toronto while wearing full cowboy chaps?
fact: The outspoken "Motor City Madman" Ted Nugent was notorious for outrageous outdoor stunts, including arriving at hotel check-ins and concert venues on horseback carrying compound hunting bows.

q: In 1965, which iconic pop singer was arrested in London for urinating against the exterior wall of a gas station after the attendant refused to let him use the private restroom?
options: All of the above (along with Bill Wyman)
fact: In March 1965, members of the Rolling Stones were stopped at the Francis Service Station in East London; after being denied the restroom, several band members relieved themselves on the wall and were fined £5 each for insulting behavior.

q: What did actor Christian Bale do when the director of photography on "Terminator Salvation" (2009) accidentally walked into his eyeline during an emotional scene?
options: Unleashed a famous, expletive-laden four-minute verbal tirade that was secretly recorded and leaked to the media
Threw a prop grenade at the lighting scaffold
Walked off the Albuquerque set and flew back to Los Angeles for three days
Challenged the cinematographer to an arm-wrestling contest in front of the crew
fact: Bale’s leaked audio rant against DP Shane Hurlbut ("Do you want me to go trash your lights?!") went viral across the world; Bale later made a sincere public apology on KROQ radio for losing his composure.

q: Which Hollywood legend was once challenged to a bare-knuckle boxing match behind an Italian restaurant by Frank Sinatra's bodyguards and knocked out two of them?
fact: World War II veteran Lee Marvin had zero patience for celebrity entourages; after a confrontation at a Palm Springs nightspot, Marvin stepped into the alley and swiftly dismantled Sinatra's security guards.

q: In 1989, which pop star was sued by the manufacturer of Pepsi after her controversial music video for "Like a Prayer" sparked a worldwide boycott by religious groups?
fact: Madonna had signed a $5 million endorsement deal with Pepsi; when the video featuring burning crosses and stigmata debuted, protests from the Vatican and conservative groups forced Pepsi to pull the ad campaign, though Madonna kept the fee.

q: What did eccentric director Werner Herzog do when his lead actor Klaus Kinski threatened to quit and abandon the production of "Aguirre, the Wrath of God"?
options: Herzog told Kinski he had a rifle with eight bullets, and that if Kinski walked, seven bullets would go into Kinski and the eighth into Herzog
Offered Kinski 50% ownership of the master camera negatives
Tied Kinski to a balsa-wood raft until he agreed to finish the scene
Threaten to feed Kinski's wardrobe to the river piranhas
fact: Herzog admitted in his documentary "My Best Fiend" that when Kinski packed his bags on the riverbank, Herzog calmly promised to shoot Kinski dead before he could reach the boat, forcing Kinski back to set.

q: In 1991, which famous musician had his passport confiscated by Italian authorities after he drove a Ferrari Testarossa through a pedestrian piazza in Florence at 90 mph?
fact: Clapton is a passionate Ferrari collector; during a high-speed tour through northern Italy in the early 1990s, local traffic police impounded his vehicle for extreme speeding in historic zones.

q: Which celebrated actor was once arrested in 1969 for climbing onto the roof of the Hollywood Palladium during an awards show and dropping ping-pong balls onto the red carpet?
fact: Hopper was at the peak of his counterculture, psychedelic rebellion following the monumental success of "Easy Rider", staging guerrilla disruptions at traditional Hollywood gatherings.

q: What did actor Christopher Walken do when he worked as a baker’s apprentice in Queens, New York, before his acting career took off?
options: Insisted on decorating every single birthday cake with a miniature chocolate dancer
Refused to touch flour unless he was wearing white silk gloves
Slept on flour sacks inside the bakery kitchen during overnight shift breaks
Spoke only to the pastries to improve their texture
fact: Walken’s family owned a popular bakery in Astoria, Queens; young Walken, who was training as a tap dancer, loved piping elaborate dancing figures onto commercial cakes and pastries.

q: In 1998, which movie star tackled a man who had snatched an elderly tourist's handbag in front of the Eiffel Tower in Paris, holding him until the Gendarmerie arrived?
fact: Brosnan, in Paris promoting a James Bond film, saw a street thief snatch a bag; he sprinted across the cobblestones, grabbed the perpetrator, and retrieved the stolen property, delighting Parisian onlookers.

q: In 1968, which legendary actor and counterculture icon was thrown out of the Cannes Film Festival after swinging from the stage curtains to prevent the festival from continuing during student protests?
fact: Directors Godard and Truffaut shut down the 1968 Cannes Film Festival in solidarity with workers and students striking across France, physically clinging to the red velvet projection curtains.

q: What bizarre medical mishap did actor George Clooney suffer while filming a brutal torture sequence for the 2005 political thriller "Syriana"?
options: A torn rotator cuff from being suspended by chains
A cracked skull and torn dura that leaked spinal fluid through his nose
A double lung collapse from breathing prop theatrical smoke
A fractured sternum from an unpadded wooden chair blow
fact: Clooney hit his head when a chair was kicked out from under him, causing a severe spinal fluid leak that caused debilitating headaches and required spinal surgeries.

q: Which rock star had his tooth knocked out by a glass beer mug thrown by a fan in 1974, then picked up the shard of glass and carved an "X" into his own chest on stage?
fact: At the final Stooges concert at the Michigan Palace in February 1974 (captured on "Metallic K.O."), Iggy Pop engaged in an all-out war with a local biker gang throwing ice, bottles, and debris.

q: In 1982, why did comedian Chevy Chase get into a physical fistfight backstage at "Saturday Night Live" with Bill Murray right before Murray stepped out to do the monologue?
options: Murray confronted Chase over abandoning the cast after Season 1, telling him his wife hated him
Chase refused to share the host's private dressing room
Chase made a disparaging remark about Murray's acne-scarred face
fact: Minutes before showtime, Murray and Chase traded insults—Murray shouting Chase was a medium talent and Chase mocking Murray's complexion—before John Belushi broke up their brawl.

q: What eccentric thing did screen legend Marlon Brando do when filming "The Score" (2001) with director Frank Oz?
options: Refused to wear pants in any scene where his waist was not visible on camera
Referred to Frank Oz exclusively as "Miss Piggy" (Oz's Muppet character)
Communicated with the crew solely using a walkie-talkie from his trailer
fact: Brando tormented Oz on set, mocking his Muppet puppeteer background, stripping off his trousers so Oz couldn't shoot wide shots, and forcing co-star Robert De Niro to direct him.

q: In 1977, which hard-rock band was arrested en masse at an arena in Cleveland after the lead guitarist fired a signal flare into the ceiling insulation during the encore?
fact: Aerosmith shows in the late 1970s were notoriously chaotic; band members and crew faced frequent arrests, venue bans, and injuries from exploding stage pyrotechnics and cherry bombs thrown by fans.

q: Which Hollywood legend was once an undercover bodyguard for Frank Sinatra and saved Sinatra from being ambushed by armed mobsters in a Las Vegas casino alley in 1960?
fact: Actor Brad Dexter famously saved Sinatra from drowning off the coast of Kauai in 1964; earlier in Las Vegas, Dexter served as Sinatra's fierce protector during organized crime disputes.

q: What did eccentric pop genius Brian Wilson do when he became convinced that the recording of the Beach Boys song "Fire" (from the "Smile" sessions) was cursed?
options: Burned the master tape boxes in a metal trash can in his backyard
Hired a brass band to play church hymns outside the studio to purge demons
Forced all studio musicians to wear toy red plastic fire helmets while tracking
fact: Wilson insisted the musicians wear fire helmets during the session; when several local buildings in Los Angeles caught fire days later, a panicked Wilson burned the master tapes.

q: In 1993, which actor broke his nose on the set of "Tombstone" when co-star Kurt Russell accidentally struck him with a prop shotgun barrel during a saloon shootout?
fact: Biehn, who played the villainous Johnny Ringo, suffered a broken nose and deep facial lacerations during an intense, fast-moving hand-to-hand fight with Russell inside the saloon set.

q: Which classic filmmaker was once challenged to a duel by an Italian movie critic in 1961, meeting at dawn in a villa garden outside Rome with real fencing epees?
fact: Luchino Visconti engaged in a formal dawn duel with critic Gian Luigi Rondi following a scathing review of his film "Rocco and His Brothers", though both escaped with only surface scratches.

q: In 1989, which rap superstar was arrested at a concert in Columbus, Georgia, for performing the anti-police anthem "Fuck tha Police" after local authorities explicitly forbade it?
fact: Police officers shut down the concert and rushed the stage; gunfire or firecrackers sounded in the arena, and members of N.W.A were detained and fined at their hotel later that night.

q: What bizarre culinary superstition did actor Nicolas Cage adopt in the 2000s regarding which animals he was willing to eat?
options: He refused to eat any animal that didn't have "dignified sex" (eating birds and fish, but avoiding pigs)
He ate only four-legged animals that grazed under a full moon
He consumed only raw sea urchin and venison on filming days
He ate exclusively food dyed black with squid ink
fact: Cage explained in an interview that he chooses which meats to eat based on how the animals mate: "I think fish are very dignified with sex, as are birds. But pigs, not so much."

q: In 1973, which rock icon threw a bowl of guacamole into the ventilation fan of an airplane cabin, covering first-class passengers and flight attendants in green avocado mush?
fact: Keith Moon's airline antics were legendary; bored on a transatlantic flight, he hurled appetizers into cabin air vents and once offered the captain $500 to let him land the plane.
